name: ADU vs Junior ADU: What’s the Difference?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an ADU and a junior ADU when planning a custom build in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between an ADU and a junior ADU when planning a custom build in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Homeowners often confuse ADUs and junior ADUs because both add living space to a property, but they serve different purposes and are built differently. A standard ADU can be detached, attached, or converted from existing space, and it functions like an independent residence. A junior ADU is typically created inside the main home, often from a bedroom or portion of the house, and is generally smaller with fewer construction changes. The right choice depends on lot size, existing floor plan, budget, rental goals, and privacy needs. In Los Angeles County, the design and permit path can also differ, so the contractor should confirm which option is most feasible before plans are finalized. Homeowners should compare build cost, rental potential, utility needs, and long-term flexibility before deciding. A contractor with ADU experience can help determine which version maximizes space without overbuilding the property.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU is a separate secondary housing unit with its own kitchen, bathroom, and living space, while a junior ADU is usually created within the footprint of the main home and is smaller and more limited. The main differences are size, privacy, utility setup, and how much structural work is needed. Local rules can also affect parking and conversion options.
